## transformers.distributed.fsdp

- `Any(*args, **kwargs)` — Special type indicating an unconstrained type.
- `CPUOffloadPolicy(pin_memory: bool = True) -> None` — This offload policy offloads parameters, gradients, and optimizer states to CPU. Sharded parameters are copied host-to-device before all-gather. The all-gathered parameters are freed according to ``reshard_after_forward``. Sharded gradients are copied device-to-host in backward, and the optimizer step runs on CPU with CPU optimizer states.
- `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None, reduce_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None, output_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None, cast_forward_inputs: bool = True) -> None` — This configures FSDP's mixed precision. Unlike autocast, this applies mixed precision at the module level, not op level, which means low-precision activations are saved for backward and high-to-low-precision casts are incurred only at module boundaries.
- `QuantizationMethod(*values)` — str(object='') -> str str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str
  - members: BITS_AND_BYTES, GPTQ, AWQ, AQLM, VPTQ, QUANTO, EETQ, HIGGS, HQQ, COMPRESSED_TENSORS, FBGEMM_FP8, TORCHAO, GGUF, BITNET, SPQR, FP8, QUARK, FPQUANT, AUTOROUND, MXFP4, NVFP4, MXFP8, METAL, FOUR_OVER_SIX, SINQ, GEMMA
- `apply_fully_sharded_data_parallelism(model: 'nn.Module', mesh_manager: 'MeshManager') -> 'nn.Module'` — Apply FSDP2 (fully_shard) to a model: dispatched experts on `efsdp` and the rest of the modules on `fsdp`.
- `expand_fsdp_plan(model: 'nn.Module', fsdp_plan: 'dict[str, str]') -> 'tuple[list[tuple[str, nn.Module]], list[tuple[str, nn.Module]]]'` — Expand plan keys into reshard and no-reshard ``(module_name, module)`` shard targets.
- `fully_shard(module, *, mesh: 'DeviceMesh | None' = None, reshard_after_forward: 'bool | int | None' = None, shard_placement_fn: 'Callable[[nn.Parameter], ShardPlacementFnResult] | None' = None, mp_policy: 'MixedPrecisionPolicy' = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=None, reduce_dtype=None, output_dtype=None, cast_forward_inputs=True), offload_policy: 'OffloadPolicy' = OffloadPolicy(), ignored_params: 'set[nn.Parameter] | None' = None, dp_mesh_dims: 'DataParallelMeshDims | None' = None)` — Apply fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP) to ``module``, where FSDP shards module parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across data parallel workers to save memory at the cost of communication.

## transformers.distributed.sharding_utils

- `DTensor(*args: _P.args, **kwargs: _P.kwargs) -> None` — ``DTensor`` (Distributed Tensor) is a subclass of ``torch.Tensor`` that provides single-device like abstraction to program with multi-device ``torch.Tensor``. It describes the distributed tensor sharding layout (DTensor Layout) through the :class:`DeviceMesh` and following types of :class:`Placement`:
- `DtensorShardOperation(param: 'DTensor')` — Shard-on-read: slice a full disk tensor down to this rank's local DTensor shard, for any combination of placements on a 1-D or n-D mesh. It's on read because instructions are made so the cpu only fetches on disk the parts we want.
- `Shard` — The ``Shard(dim)`` placement describes the DTensor sharding on tensor dimension ``dim`` over a corresponding ``DeviceMesh`` dimension, where each rank on the DeviceMesh dimension only holds a shard/piece of the global Tensor. The ``Shard(dim)`` placement follows the ``torch.chunk(dim)`` semantic, where the last few shards on the DeviceMesh dimension might be empty when the tensor dimension is not 
- `compute_local_shape_and_global_offset(global_shape: torch.Size | list[int] | tuple[int, ...], mesh: torch.distributed.device_mesh.DeviceMesh, placements: collections.abc.Sequence[torch.distributed.tensor.placement_types.Placement], skip_offset: bool = False) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]` — Compute the local tensor shape and the global offsets into the original tensor of a DTensor on its current global rank. This is useful for checkpointing purpose.

## transformers.distributed.tensor_parallel

- `AllReduceParallel()` — All-reduce a module's partial forward output across the TP mesh.
- `Callable()` — class
- `ColwiseParallel(*, input_layouts=None, output_layouts=None, use_local_output: 'bool' = True)` — Column-wise: weight & bias → Shard(0) (Embedding: Shard(1)); input replicated, output Shard(-1).
- `DTensor(*args: _P.args, **kwargs: _P.kwargs) -> None` — ``DTensor`` (Distributed Tensor) is a subclass of ``torch.Tensor`` that provides single-device like abstraction to program with multi-device ``torch.Tensor``. It describes the distributed tensor sharding layout (DTensor Layout) through the :class:`DeviceMesh` and following types of :class:`Placement`:
- `EpDispatchExpertsParallel()` — Dispatch disjoint TP token slices to the experts' owners, then replicate the combined output on TP.
- `EpRouterParallel()` — Expert-parallel router: forward-only slicing of router outputs to local experts.
- `GeneralInterface()` — Dict-like object keeping track of a class-wide mapping, as well as a local one. Allows to have library-wide modifications through the class mapping, as well as local modifications in a single file with the local mapping.
- `MlaKvAProjParallel()` — For MLA attention used in DeepSeek-V2 style models (deepseek_v2, longcat_flash, glm_moe_dsa, glm4_moe_lite): kv_a_proj_with_mqa output is [kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim] (can have different naming but important thing to understand is that it is split) Example below (from modeling_longcat_flash.py):
- `MoEParamShard(placement, *, shards_expert_dim: 'bool' = False)` — Param-only EP style for MoE expert weights (``grouped_gemm``).
- `MoeExpertsParallel()` — class
- `MoeIdentityParallel()` — Used in longcat_flash zero_experts (nn.Identity) which return the same value on every GPU, but the moe_tp_experts will sums across GPUs. Therefore we pre-divide the identity input by tp_size to cancel the extra scaling.
- `MoeTensorParalellMegaMoeExperts()` — TP layer for DeepGEMM Mega MoE experts.
- `PackedColwiseParallel(*, use_local_output: 'bool' = True, split_factor: 'int' = 2)` — Column-wise parallel style for fused linear weights packed along the output dimension.
- `PackedRowwiseParallel(*, split_factor: 'int' = 2)` — Parameter style for fused weights packed along the final dimension.
- `ParallelInterface()` — Registry of named TP styles for the DTensor backend.
- `Partial` — The base class for the Placement type, where it describes how a DTensor is placed onto the ``DeviceMesh``. ``Placement`` and ``DeviceMesh`` together could describe the DTensor Layout. It is the base class of the three main DTensor Placement types: ``Shard``, ``Replicate``, and ``Partial``.
- `Replicate` — The ``Replicate()`` placement describes the DTensor replicating on a corresponding ``DeviceMesh`` dimension, where each rank on the DeviceMesh dimension holds a replica of the global Tensor. The ``Replicate`` placement can be used by all DTensor APIs (i.e. ``distribute_tensor``, ``DTensor.from_local``, etc.)
- `ReplicatedWithGradAllReduce()` — Replicated parameter whose gradient is partial.
- `RouterParallelMegaMoe()` — Router TP plan used with DeepGEMM Mega MoE.
- `RowwiseParallel(*, input_layouts=None, output_layouts=None, use_local_output: 'bool' = True)` — Row-wise: weight → Shard(1), bias → Replicate (Embedding: weight → Shard(0)).
- `SequenceParallel(*, sequence_dim: 'int' = 1, use_local_output: 'bool' = True)` — class
- `Shard` — The ``Shard(dim)`` placement describes the DTensor sharding on tensor dimension ``dim`` over a corresponding ``DeviceMesh`` dimension, where each rank on the DeviceMesh dimension only holds a shard/piece of the global Tensor. The ``Shard(dim)`` placement follows the ``torch.chunk(dim)`` semantic, where the last few shards on the DeviceMesh dimension might be empty when the tensor dimension is not
